body_text:

subject: ASC 606 treatment for annual license deals
snippet: Aditi, Working through the Vantage Foundries deal ($184,000 annual license plus a bundled install/config service) and I want to make sure we're recognizing it right before I book J
body_text:
Aditi,

Working through the Vantage Foundries deal ($184,000 annual license plus a bundled install/config service) and I want to make sure we're recognizing it right before I book July revenue. Do we treat the whole thing as one performance obligation recognized ratably, or split the install service out and recognize that point-in-time when it's done? The SOW doesn't separately price the install, it's just bundled into the $184K.

Want to get this right before close, not after.

Karen

meta.action_summary: Determine ASC 606 revenue recognition treatment for the Vantage Foundries bundle before July close.
meta.notes: Precise technical question, sets up Aditi's numbers-forward answer.

subject: Re: ASC 606 treatment for annual license deals
snippet: Karen, They're two distinct performance obligations even though they're bundled in one price — the install/config service is capable of being distinct and isn't a significant integ
body_text:
Karen,

They're two distinct performance obligations even though they're bundled in one price — the install/config service is capable of being distinct and isn't a significant integration or customization of the license itself (ASC 606-10-25-19). So: allocate the $184,000 using relative standalone selling price. Our standard install rate is roughly $8,000 for a deal this size based on the last three comparable installs, which leaves $176,000 for the license.

License: recognize ratably over the 12-month term, $14,666.67/month starting on the contract start date.
Install: recognize point-in-time when the install is complete and accepted, not when it's scheduled.

If install isn't done by month-end, none of that $8,000 hits July — don't accrue it early. I'll update the revenue recognition memo with this determination by end of week so we have it documented for Nadia's team too.

Aditi

meta.action_summary: Gave Karen the ASC 606 allocation and recognition treatment for the Vantage Foundries bundle.
meta.commitment_made_by_user: I'll update the revenue recognition memo with this determination by end of week
meta.notes: Precise, citation-backed, numbers-forward — restates the mechanics before landing the answer.

subject: July close recap and FY27 budget kickoff
snippet: Team, July close is final as of yesterday, and I want to give everyone the same picture before we start FY27 budget season, since the two are related. **July results.** Revenue cam
body_text:
Team,

July close is final as of yesterday, and I want to give everyone the same picture before we start FY27 budget season, since the two are related.

**July results.** Revenue came in at $1.42M against a budget of $1.38M, driven mostly by the Vantage Foundries install landing three weeks earlier than planned. Gross margin was 41.6%, up from June's 41.2% once you strip out the one-time items I flagged to Sam last week. Cash on hand is $2.31M as of July 31, and burn was $187K for the month against a budgeted $210K — mostly timing on the two open engineering reqs that haven't started yet. Nothing in the July numbers changes our runway math: we're still at roughly 14 months at current burn, 11 months if both reqs fill in September as planned.

**Where FY27 budget season starts.** I'm kicking off the FY27 model this week. Timeline: department heads submit inputs by August 14, I build the first consolidated draft by August 21, we review as a group August 24-25, and I need a board-ready number in hand before our next board meeting. That's a tight two and a half weeks, so I'd rather get rough numbers from you on time than perfect numbers late — we can refine in the review sessions.

**What I need from each of you specifically.** Karen — final July actuals and the audit PBC list status, since Nadia's team starts fieldwork August 11 and I want the two processes to not collide. Derek — FY27 sales quota and territory plan, plus your read on the Vantage Foundries expansion opportunity since that alone could move the revenue line by six figures. Ruth — headcount and capex plan for ops, including whether the Peabody line automation project gets greenlit in FY27 or slips again. Hannah — headcount actuals as of July 31 with fully-loaded cost, which I've already asked for separately but flagging here too since it's the backbone of the whole model.

A few principles I'd like us to hold to this cycle: build from actual unit economics rather than growing every line by a flat percentage, flag any assumption that depends on a deal that hasn't closed yet, and keep the model in the shared template so I'm not reconciling five different spreadsheet formats in week three like last year.

I'll circulate the finalized FY27 budget calendar by August 14 with specific review slots for each of you. Questions before then, just grab time on my calendar.

Thanks all — good close, let's keep the momentum into budget season.

Aditi

meta.action_summary: Communicated July close results and kicked off FY27 budget season with a submission calendar.
meta.commitment_made_by_user: I'll circulate the finalized FY27 budget calendar by August 14
meta.notes: Long-form strategic update to the leadership team.

subject: FY27 budget build — assumptions and timeline
snippet: Sam, Before department inputs start rolling in, I want to align with you on the top-level assumptions I'm planning to use for the FY27 model, since these will shape everything unde
body_text:
Sam,

Before department inputs start rolling in, I want to align with you on the top-level assumptions I'm planning to use for the FY27 model, since these will shape everything under them.

**Revenue.** Base case assumes we hold current customer ARR flat plus 12% net expansion from existing accounts (Vantage Foundries and Tarrow-scale customers upgrading tiers), plus $1.8M in new logo revenue based on Derek's current pipeline coverage of 3.2x quota. I'm deliberately not baking in the two enterprise deals still in legal review — if either closes it's upside, not baseline.

**Gross margin.** Modeling 42.5%, a full point above FY26's blended 41.2%, driven by the Peabody line automation project reducing freight and labor cost per unit if it gets funded in the capex plan. If that project doesn't get greenlit, margin assumption drops back to 41.5%.

**Headcount.** Planning for 12 net new hires across the year, weighted toward engineering (5) and sales (4), with the rest split across ops and G&A. Fully-loaded cost per hire averaging $142K based on this year's actuals. This is the single biggest lever in the model — every 2 hires we add or cut moves burn by roughly $24K/month.

**Cash and runway.** Starting cash of $2.31M (July 31 actual) plus whatever we draw on the renewed credit facility — I'm in the middle of negotiating better terms with Harborline, aiming to close by August 31. Base case burn under these assumptions runs about $165K/month, which gets us to roughly 16 months of runway without a new raise, assuming the facility renews as expected.

**Capex.** $340K planned, almost entirely the Peabody automation project ($280K) plus normal IT refresh ($60K). This is the one line I think deserves real debate before we lock it — it's a big number for a company our size and I want Ruth's ROI case in writing before it goes in the base case rather than a stretch scenario.

Timeline: department inputs due August 14, first consolidated draft August 21, group review August 24-25. I'll have the first full model in your inbox by August 3rd — sorry, meant August 21st, fixing that typo before anyone holds me to the wrong date. Let me know if any of these top-level assumptions don't match your read before I lock them in as the base case for everyone else's inputs.

One more thing worth flagging now rather than in week three: last year's model fell apart a bit at the review stage because each department was implicitly assuming a different revenue number when they built their own headcount and spend requests. I'd like to send everyone the same top-level revenue and margin assumptions above before they start their own inputs, specifically so Derek's sales hiring plan and Ruth's capex request are both built against the same base case rather than three different optimistic versions of the year. If you're fine with the assumptions as I've laid them out, I'll send this same memo to Karen, Derek, Ruth, and Hannah on Monday as the starting point for their submissions, and note explicitly that anything they want to flex above this baseline needs a one-line justification I can defend to the board.

Aditi

meta.action_summary: Circulated FY27 top-level budget assumptions for Sam's sign-off before department inputs start.
meta.commitment_made_by_user: I'll have the first full model in your inbox by August 21st
meta.notes: Long-form budget memo with a self-corrected date typo, left in deliberately for realism.

Ahead of fieldwork starting August 11, here's where we stand on the full PBC list. I've grouped by status so your team can plan around what's ready versus what's still coming.

- Q4 bank confirmations
- AP and AR aging as of June 30
- Revenue recognition memo, including the ASC 606 treatment we finalized for bundled license/install deals
- Payroll register and benefits reconciliation for the year
- Board meeting minutes for FY26 (four meetings)
- Insurance certificates, all lines

**Coming this week:**
- Lease amortization schedule (Wednesday)
- Related-party disclosures, including the $40,000 loan from Sam to the company in March, fully documented with the promissory note (Wednesday)
- Inventory count reconciliation for the Peabody warehouse (Thursday, waiting on Ruth's team to finish the physical count)

**Open questions I'd like to flag before fieldwork rather than have your team discover them:**
- The Harborline credit facility is mid-renewal. Terms aren't final, so the going-concern and subsequent-events disclosure language may need to stay flexible until late August.
- We changed our sales commission accrual methodology in Q3 to better match commission timing to revenue recognition. I have a memo explaining the change and its immaterial impact, want to make sure your team agrees with 'immaterial' before we finalize.
- Meridian Fasteners invoice dispute ($2,300) is still open as of today — it's sitting in disputed AP, not yet resolved either way.

One more item for context rather than action: we're mid-negotiation on the Harborline credit facility renewal, and I expect the final terms to land somewhere around SOFR+225 to SOFR+250 with the minimum cash covenant replaced by a debt service coverage ratio. I don't think this changes anything materially for the FY26 audit itself since it's a subsequent event either way, but I wanted your team to have the full picture rather than finding a half-finished negotiation thread buried in my email if it comes up in confirmations.

On staffing for fieldwork: Miles will be your main point of contact for anything AP/AR related, Karen for the general ledger and revenue recognition questions, and I'll take related-party, the credit facility, and anything that needs a judgment call rather than a lookup. If your team prefers a single point of contact instead of three, I can coordinate that on our end so you're not chasing three different people for status updates during the two weeks of fieldwork.

Let me know if the grouping works for your fieldwork plan or if there's a different sequencing you'd prefer. Happy to get on a call with Karen and Miles before Monday if useful.

Aditi Sharma
VP Finance, Northwind Robotics

subject: Net-60 terms — not this cycle
snippet: Hi Priya, Thanks for putting the Net-60 request in writing. I understand the ask, but I'm not able to move Ironforge to Net-60 right now — we standardized all suppliers on Net-30 l
body_text:
Hi Priya,

Thanks for putting the Net-60 request in writing. I understand the ask, but I'm not able to move Ironforge to Net-60 right now — we standardized all suppliers on Net-30 last year specifically so we weren't carrying inconsistent payment terms across the vendor book, and making an exception here would mean fielding the same request from three other suppliers who asked and were told no. If cash flow timing is the underlying issue, I'm open to talking about a different structure — split invoicing, or a small early-payment discount in exchange for staying on Net-30 — but a blanket extension isn't something I can do.

Happy to get on a call if useful.

Aditi Sharma
VP Finance, Northwind Robotics

meta.action_summary: Declined Ironforge's request to move to Net-60 payment terms.
meta.notes: Rejection — polite but immovable, offers an alternative.

subject: Ramp annual renewal — pushing back on the fee increase
snippet: Hi Devon, Saw the renewal quote came in with a 22% increase on the platform fee versus last year, from $9,600 to $11,712. We've grown card spend through Ramp by about 15% over the
body_text:
Hi Devon,

Saw the renewal quote came in with a 22% increase on the platform fee versus last year, from $9,600 to $11,712. We've grown card spend through Ramp by about 15% over the same period, so some increase makes sense, but 22% on the platform fee alone is more than I can justify without pushing back. What can you do closer to a 10-12% increase, especially given we're coming up on renewal for the expense management module too and I'd rather bundle the conversation than negotiate twice.

Happy to hop on a call this week if that's easier than going back and forth by email.

Aditi Sharma
VP Finance, Northwind Robotics

meta.action_summary: Pushed back on Ramp's 22% renewal fee increase, countering at 10-12%.

subject: Vantage Foundries payment terms — final answer
snippet: Hi Priya, To restate what you're asking: Net-45 instead of the Net-30 in the MSA, given your AP cycle runs on a 6-week close. I understand the reasoning, but Net-30 is standard acr
body_text:
Hi Priya,

To restate what you're asking: Net-45 instead of the Net-30 in the MSA, given your AP cycle runs on a 6-week close. I understand the reasoning, but Net-30 is standard across our customer book and I'd rather not create precedent, especially on an account this size where other customers would notice if terms weren't consistent. What I can offer instead is a 1.5% discount for payment within 15 days, which nets out better for you than Net-45 would cost us in DSO — happy to run the math together if useful. Let me know if that works on your end.

Aditi Sharma
VP Finance, Northwind Robotics

meta.action_summary: Declined Vantage Foundries' Net-45 request, offered an early-payment discount instead.
